title: Adapting Large Language Models for Education: Foundational Capabilities, Potentials, and Challenges
extended_summary:
This paper is a survey of large language model (LLM) capabilities relevant to education, rather than an empirical study of a classroom intervention. It asks how LLMs can support educational tasks and what technical limitations remain before they can serve as effective intelligent education systems.

The paper reviews five foundational capability areas: mathematics, writing, programming, reasoning, and knowledge-based question answering. For each area, it summarizes representative methods, benchmarks, and current performance, and it discusses whether the methods generalize toward broader educational use. The paper also contrasts two system-level architectures for educational LLMs: a unified model and a mixture-of-experts approach.

The context is online education and intelligent tutoring, with emphasis on student-facing question answering and problem solving rather than teacher coaching or lesson-plan feedback. No participant population is studied, and no intervention is implemented. The main conclusion is that LLMs show strong promise for education, but important challenges remain, especially hallucination, weak mathematical reasoning, over-correction in writing support, limited interpretability in programming, and the need for better integration of external tools and educational knowledge.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: A general large language model / generative AI system used for educational tasks such as answering questions, generating text, summarizing, correcting grammar, coding assistance, and reasoning.
identified_tools.use_case: This is a survey paper that reviews the capabilities, potentials, and challenges of LLMs for education rather than evaluating one specific product in a single intervention.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a conceptual/survey paper that synthesizes literature on LLM capabilities in education. It does not report a primary empirical study, RCT, or meta-analytic estimate for a specific tool.
impact_tier_rationale: No intervention effects, effect sizes, or outcome estimates are reported. The paper discusses potential applications and challenges rather than measured impact.
